summary: A 1932 Forest Service L-4 cabin above timberline on Mount Baker, unstaffed since 1961 and maintained by the Skagit Alpine Club, reached by a 3.5-mile trail from Park Butte Trailhead.

facts.design: L-4 live-in cabin, 14 x 14 ft, with catwalk

access.note: Forest Service lists the site open 24 hours a day, first come first served; a recreation pass is required at the trailhead May 1 to Oct 31; no fee for the site. Inside Mount Baker Wilderness, with wilderness rules.

visit.trail_note: Trail 603 from the Park Butte Trailhead; the nomination describes a 3.5-mile Forest Service trail to the lookout.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District)

events.note: Built in the fall of 1932 by a small Forest Service crew (C.A. Larsen, William Thompson, a hired carpenter); packer Roy Evans brought in the materials. Firelookout.com gives 1933 (see corrections).
Last regular fire-detection use; firelookout.com says last manned in the 1960s
Skagit Alpine Club took over the lookout under a special use permit with the Forest Service and has maintained it for recreation since

In the 1970s, when Mount Baker threatened to erupt, the restored lookout served as an observatory for volcano monitors (NHLR; the Skagit Alpine Club says a University of California camera was installed in the mid-1970s)
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on December 1, 2003

corrections.why: The NRHP nomination gives 1932, with the builders' concrete inscriptions dated 1932 and a 1932 plan. The NHLR register and the Forest Service page also give 1932. Only firelookout.com gives 1933.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 5,369 ft (1,636 m); the nomination gives about 5,400 ft; the Forest Service gives 5,300 ft. The record's 1636.5 m matches NHLR and is kept.
NHLR says the club has maintained the lookout since then, after fire use ended in 1961; the NRHP nomination dates the club special use permit to 1962. The story uses 1962 from the nomination.

No current staff is named. The Forest Service and the Skagit Alpine Club say volunteers maintain the lookout; the nomination says it was last used for fire detection in 1961. Record treated as unstaffed.

notes_for_editor: Build year: the brief's 1933 comes only from firelookout.com. The NRHP nomination (inscriptions dated 1932, 1932 plan), NHLR and Forest Service all say 1932; correction proposed. Staffing: fire detection ended 1961; volunteers have maintained it under a Skagit Alpine Club special use permit since 1962. The 1970s volcano-monitoring use and the WWII plane-spotter role come from NHLR and club history; the WWII plane-spotter claim is confirmed on the club page (early 1940s). Access: the Forest Service page lists first-come, first-served use, no site fee, a recreation pass at the trailhead May 1 to Oct 31, and wilderness rules; the NHLR lists it as available for rental, which may be a different booking channel, not checked. Firelookout.com credits photos to the Fire Lookout Museum and Tammy McLeod, but no image URLs were captured, so no photo entries were added. Elevation conflicts are minor and the record's value matches NHLR. Confidence is high on build year and access, but the rental wording is not verified.
